# Knowledge map: Live hardware observations and peripheral contracts

<!-- Generated by `python -m tools.research.knowledge_map build` from `docs/map/sources/hardware-live.toml`. Do not edit by hand. -->

- **Scope:** Read-only observations of the physical ILCE-6400: GPIO, bus power, HDMI/CEC, touch input, display/OSD, GPES BAR, MISCREG and the /dev/mem safety boundary, lens interface.
- **Evidence span:** E0068-E0075, E0084, E0297-E0298, E0313-E0314, E0647-E0649; last reviewed 2026-11-26.
- **Deep review:** 15 of 21 records read in full and checked claim by claim ([curation plan](CURATION_PLAN.md)); the rest are curated from titles, lead paragraphs and consolidated documents.
- **Status legend:** PHYSICAL = observed on the camera/host; OFFLINE = disassembly, Unicorn or static proof; INFERENCE = argued from evidence, not observed directly; RETRACTED/REFUTED = do not rely on, kept to prevent re-derivation.

The evidence records are authoritative; follow the links before acting on a claim.

## Frontier

### <a id="f01"></a>F01 - Reserved first MiB: what is at 0x000F8000 and what else may be read?

- **State:** `blocked-on-user-go`
- **Candidate:** ro_page v2 (529,412 bytes, SHA-256 8c9f360b...5c64) with catching=True, one 4 KiB page per boot.
- **Verified so far:** Same FSR 0x008 fault as the reboot, caught as signal 7 on the camera with uptime 3,198.8 -> 3,243.9 s; not a map of the window.
- **Next:** Bound the first-MiB window with a per-address go-ahead, one page per boot, starting far from 0xF8000; DRAM and read() on /dev/mem stay forbidden.
- **Read in the result:** The user-mode fault is reported and caught, the exception monitor stays silent, /proc/uptime remains monotonic, and the page decodes as a device or SRAM page rather than returning zeros.
- **Evidence:** [E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md)

### <a id="f02"></a>F02 - Sigma lens capability through a passive mount-bus capture

- **State:** `not-started`
- **Next:** Find the receiver or store of the 0xA2AFEC notifications (candidates: libIMDB and the large anonymous im.elf objects), or read MakerNote LensE-mountVersion and lens firmware fields from host-side JPEGs; compare a Sigma body with the TTArtisan first-generation-only set.
- **Read in the result:** The bitmap at BL_LENS_DATA+1 names the second-generation IDs, or the MakerNote values predict which command set the body uses.
- **Evidence:** [E0648](../evidence/0648-ilce6400-bl-lens-focus-command-ids.md), [E0649](../evidence/0649-ilce6400-live-lens-info-linux-side-negative.md)

## Hazards (read before any camera run)

| ID | Hazard | Effect | Rule | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="h01"></a>H01 | Reading /dev/stream for OSD capture | The camera rebooted during the OSD probe. | Never read /dev/stream for capture; use host-side ptrace of im.elf's existing mapping (E0298). | [E0297](../evidence/0297-live-display-contract-and-camera-reboot.md), [E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md) |
| <a id="h02"></a>H02 | Unvetted /dev/mem pages | External abort on PA 0x000F8000 warm-rebooted the camera. | Every /dev/mem access passes tools/devmem_policy.py; never bulk-scan physical memory or read DRAM through /dev/mem. | [E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md) |
| <a id="h03"></a>H03 | Bulk /dev/mem physical scan | A 16 MiB-chunk /dev/mem scan dropped the camera's USB and rebooted it (uptime reset to 61 s); the camera recovered with no persistent change. | Bulk physical sweeps are excluded from the standing read-only allowance. Only bounded single-page reads with a policy go-ahead, /proc, /sys and kallsyms views are allowed; a bulk scan needs explicit per-incident user approval. | [E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md), [E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md) |
| <a id="h04"></a>H04 | Uncaught external abort in a /dev/mem reader | A user-mode external abort with no SIGBUS handler reaches the default core-dump path and em_exception_monitor, which warm-reboots the body even though the fault was precise. | Any reader of a GO page must install SIGBUS/SIGSEGV handling (ro_page v2, catching=True) and report the caught fault; imprecise aborts and kernel-mode faults (read() on /dev/mem) cannot be caught and stay forbidden. | [E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md) |

### <a id="dev-gpio-buspower"></a>GPIO and USB bus-power drivers

`dev.gpio-buspower` | device | inventory `kernel.modules:usb_buspwr`, `kernel.modules:usbg_buspower`

GPIO driver contract and the USB bus-power kernel modules seen during L3 bring-up.

Current knowledge:

- **C01** `OFFLINE` The GPIO driver contract and the USB bus-power driver contract are modelled; L3 execution passes 100 million instructions at that boundary. ([E0068](../evidence/0068-gpio-contract-and-usbg-buspower-module-boundary.md), [E0069](../evidence/0069-usb-buspower-driver-contract-and-100m-instruction-milestone.md))

- **C09** `OFFLINE` The setting overlay, media detection and the USB event driver contract were modelled. ([E0071](../evidence/0071-setting-overlay-media-detection-and-usb-event-boundary.md))
- **C11** `OFFLINE` GPIO is character 240:0. libul_GpioCtrl.so issues GPIO_CMD_SET_MODE 0xc0104702 through libResourceBluetooth.so; execution then maps usbg_buspower.ko (14,068 bytes, SHA-256 81fee5ccc6b14bc9f46e7f8315308b2476ba056763bf16e84ccaf053e38cea41) and stops at init_module (r7=128) at 81,686,763 instructions. ([E0068](../evidence/0068-gpio-contract-and-usbg-buspower-module-boundary.md))

### <a id="dev-touch-input"></a>Touch panel and input event nodes

`dev.touch-input` | device | inventory `kernel.modules:input`

Current knowledge:

- **C10** `PHYSICAL` The live /dev lists input event nodes 13:64, 13:65 and 13:66, but all three opened with errno 19 (ENODEV) and /proc/bus/input/devices had no entries; E0084's assignment of the nodes to a working digitizer, buttons and dials is unsupported. - **C39** `OFFLINE` The six-byte prologue 98 b5 00 af 04 46 appears 375 times in libObj executable segments, so it is not a function identity and a patch at its first match proves byte modification only. PAS_MenuSelectMode::setTouchable is at linked 0x56dcb0; its two-byte CBZ at +6 must survive, because the old four-byte NOP also overwrote the following LDR.W and left 08 31 (ADD). ([E0085](../evidence/0085-touch-hook-false-matches-and-live-disable.md), [E0086](../evidence/0086-live-touch-enodev-and-menu-instruction-audit.md))

Do not rely on:

- ~~The live touch subsystem exposes input event nodes; the camera communication architecture was recorded from the running body.~~ **C04** `RETRACTED` ([E0084](../evidence/0084-live-hardware-touch-subsystem-and-input-event-architecture.md)); see C10: The live /dev lists input event nodes 13:64, 13:65 and 13:66, but all three opened with errno 19 (ENODEV) and /proc/bus/input/devices had no entries; E0084's assignment of the nodes to a working digitizer, buttons and dials is unsupported. *Note: E0085 shows the pattern scanner patched many unrelated functions, and E0086 records ENODEV on all three event nodes with an empty input registry. The nodes exist; a working touch subsystem is not established.*

### <a id="dev-osd-display"></a>OSD A/B display planes

`dev.osd-display` | device

Two 640x480 RGBA4444 OSD planes at PA 0x23A80000 (A) and 0x23B16000 (B); captured safely through im.elf's existing mapping via ptrace.

Aliases: `640x480 RGBA4444`, `0x23A80000`, `0x23B16000`

Current knowledge:

- **C03** `PHYSICAL` Live hardware ground truth and boot telemetry were read from an ILCE-6400, including a native tally REC frame milestone. ([E0073](../evidence/0073-live-hardware-ground-truth-and-a6400-boot-telemetry.md), [E0074](../evidence/0074-native-hardware-tally-frame-milestone.md))
- **C05** `PHYSICAL` OSD A/B (640x480 RGBA4444) can be captured safely through im.elf's existing mapping with ptrace; the Sugilite buffer is not a display. ([E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md))
- **C20** `PHYSICAL` OSD A/B are 640x480 RGBA4444 (bits 12-15 red, 8-11 green, 4-7 blue, 0-3 alpha); opaque red is 0xF00F, a 32-bit pixel pair is 0xF00FF00F, and each buffer is 614,400 bytes at PA 0x23a80000 (A) and 0x23b16000 (B) with stride 0x96000. Scan-out alternates A/B at 60 Hz, so painting only A produces 30 Hz flicker. ([E0074](../evidence/0074-native-hardware-tally-frame-milestone.md))
- **C21** `PHYSICAL` A ptrace read of im.elf's existing /dev/stream mapping returned OSD A as 614,400 bytes with 607,746 nonzero and SHA-256 7a535b09be2e370fda25091a3819289bf59d8f23e82ec0bb8030a43768c32906, which decodes to a complete PlayMemories screen; OSD B returned the identical length and SHA-256, so both buffers held the same frame. ([E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md))
- **C22** `PHYSICAL` gl_common+0x1000 (PA 0x202e1000, 1,036,800 bytes) held 604,162 nonzero bytes with SHA-256 903f6910878ea1d11dc07a5b0e47b0a86ba58ca650aa700415a8557eae100b04 and decodes as a repeated pattern, not a UI frame; the 960x540 buffer is internal, not a display surface. ([E0297](../evidence/0297-live-display-contract-and-camera-reboot.md), [E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md))

Do not rely on:

- ~~The live display contract from E0297 (display buffer identification).~~ **R01** `RETRACTED` ([E0297](../evidence/0297-live-display-contract-and-camera-reboot.md)); see C05: OSD A/B (640x480 RGBA4444) can be captured safely through im.elf's existing mapping with ptrace; the Sugilite buffer is not a display. *Note: E0297 carries an explicit 'Superseded display claim' pointer to E0298.*

### <a id="dev-gpes-bar"></a>GPES BAR (SMAPH-S30) at 0xF1000000

`dev.gpes-bar` | device | address `0xF1000000`

128 KiB GPU register window: identity word 0x000b0000, IRQ status at +0x34, acks at +0x1000/+0xC18/+0x1C/+0x3C/+0x44, command block +0xE8..+0x170.

Current knowledge:

- **C06** `PHYSICAL` A read-only physical observation of the GPES BAR, GRM state and OSAL tables decoded the BAR/IRQ contract used by the opt-in engine-completion model. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md), [E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md))
- **C24** `OFFLINE` GPES BAR at 0xF1000000: +0x00 identity, +0x10/+0x14 engine counters, +0x1C acks status 0x04000000, +0x34 IRQ status, +0x3C/+0x44 ack status&0x0F, +0xC0 kick (arg|0x20000000), +0x1000/+0xC18 ack 0x40000000, and +0xE8..+0x170 is a command ring (header +0xE8, 0x80-byte descriptor at +0xF4). IRQ 0x658 reads +0x34, performs those acks and wakes dev+0x4C. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md), [E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md))
- **C25** `PHYSICAL` A read-only mmap of 0xF1000000 returned identity word +0x00 = 0x000b0000 with +0x34, +0x38, +0x3c, +0x44, +0xc0, +0xc18 and +0x1000 idle at 0; the engine counters read 0x0405C040 and 0x0406EC40, and IRQ 76 (dmpgles2) had fired 1,107,089 times while fusb_usb_vbus (230) had 6 and fusb_usb_id (231) had 0. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md), [E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md))
- **C26** `PHYSICAL` A 2,000,000-read poll of BAR+0x34 saw 1,285 nonzero values and exactly two distinct values: 0x40000000 (793 times) and 0x80000000 (492 times); no other bit was caught. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md))
- **C27** `OFFLINE` The 0xC0048203 event wait requires mask & 0xC4000000, checks [dev+0xA8] and returns the status word. The 0xC004820D ctx wait's fast flag (ctx+0x10) is written only by the guest 0x820E signal handler, and its completion word (ctx+0x14) only by 0x820E, open or release; the IRQ never completes a guest ctx, so the hardware-log wait needs a guest 0x820E. ([E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md))
- **C28** `OFFLINE` The opt-in --gles-engine-model command-completion replays the physically observed 0x40000000 IRQ class after the guest submits the BAR command (BAR+0xE8=1, +0xEA=5), performs the decoded acks and consumes the ring header; it never completes a guest ctx and injects no signal. In engine11 the guest exited the 0x72B660 loop, issued a second 0x820E and parked at 0x72BAF0. ([E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md))
- **C30** `PHYSICAL` /proc/149/mem reads of the BAR mapping return EIO and dd reads of /dev/mem at 0xF1000000 return EFAULT, while a read-only mmap of the same page works; the physical BAR probe therefore used mmap(PROT_READ) on one 4 KiB page. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md))

### <a id="policy-devmem"></a>/dev/mem access policy

`policy.devmem` | process

Single-page /dev/mem reads are gated by tools/devmem_policy.py: verified pages only, per-address go-ahead for device/SRAM pages, DRAM and bulk reads forbidden; first-MiB pages need catching=True plus a go-ahead.

Aliases: `PA 0x000F8000`, `devmem_policy.py`

Current knowledge:

- **C07** `PHYSICAL` A single-page /dev/mem read of PA 0x000F8000 returned an AXI external abort that Sony's exception monitor turned into a warm reboot; the kernel does not guard /dev/mem. ([E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md))
- **C30** `PHYSICAL` /proc/149/mem reads of the BAR mapping return EIO and dd reads of /dev/mem at 0xF1000000 return EFAULT, while a read-only mmap of the same page works; the physical BAR probe therefore used mmap(PROT_READ) on one 4 KiB page. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md))
- **C31** `PHYSICAL` tools/devmem_policy.py allows only 0xF2915000 as a standing page; device-map pages and SRAM need a per-address go-ahead; the reserved first MiB and DRAM are forbidden; multi-page ranges, unaligned addresses and read()/write() on /dev/mem, /dev/kmem or /dev/stream are forbidden. With catching=True the first MiB and undecoded holes become per-address GO. ([E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md))
- **C32** `OFFLINE` The kernel does not guard /dev/mem: there is no STRICT_DEVMEM devmem_is_allowed symbol, valid_mmap_phys_addr_range (0x601180EC) accepts any range below 4 GiB, and phys_mem_access_prot_allowed (0x6011F550) acts on conflicts only when mmap.debug != 0. /sys/module/mmap/parameters/debug reads 0 on the camera. ([E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md))
- **C33** `PHYSICAL` A single-page read of PA 0x000F8000 faults with FSR 0x008 (external abort on non-linefetch). Uncaught, it reaches force_sig_info(SIGBUS), the default core-dump path and em_exception_monitor, which warm-reboots; ro_page v2 with SIGBUS handling reported 'bus error caught: signal 7' at 0x000F8000 and the camera stayed up (uptime 3,198.8 -> 3,243.9 s). Imprecise aborts and kernel-mode faults still reboot. ([E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md))

### <a id="dev-lens"></a>Body-lens (BL) interface

`dev.lens` | device

Body-lens focus command IDs, the capability bitmap at BL_LENS_DATA+1, the body mask that admits 0x41-0x4A for any lens, and the three-bit 0x1D mode; the TTArtisan lens implements only the legacy items.

Aliases: `BL_LENS_DATA`, `0x642FE7B8`, `capability gate`, `0x63855F94`

Current knowledge:

- **C08** `PHYSICAL` Body-lens focus command IDs and a capability gate exist; with a Sigma 18-50 F2.8 DC DN attached, lens capability data is not readable from the Linux side. ([E0648](../evidence/0648-ilce6400-bl-lens-focus-command-ids.md), [E0649](../evidence/0649-ilce6400-live-lens-info-linux-side-negative.md))
- **C40** `OFFLINE` The capability bitmap is 32 bytes at BL_LENS_DATA+1 (bit id-1) and is intersected per query with a body mask at 0x63F0439B that allows 0x01-0x4C and 0x4E-0x5C for every lens; the only identity block is a three-ID inhibit. The 0x1D record carries a three-bit mode with wire values 0, 3, 4 and 6, so E0648's 'bit 2 flag' is mode bit 2, and the 0x09 STARTUP_INFO item carries status only, not the bitmap. ([E0718](../evidence/0718-ilce6400-bl-gate-bitmap-and-1d-mode.md))
- **C41** `OFFLINE` The TTArtisan AF 35/1.8 II E implements eight frame IDs plus the legacy items 0x1C/0x1D/0x1F/0x22/0x2E/0x2F/0x3C/0x3D, has no handler or reply for 0x41-0x4A, ignores the 0x1D mode byte, ships no capability bitmap or lens ID, and runs a controller with no deadband whose settle test requires exact position equality; the container encoding is undecoded, so no .fir can currently be rebuilt. ([E0719](../evidence/0719-ttartisan-af35-command-surface-and-patch-feasibility.md))
- **C35** `OFFLINE` Body-lens frames use a 0x320-byte slot with an item count at +0x18 and item pointers from +0x1C. Second-generation focus IDs are 0x41 POS_CYCLE_A, 0x43 MOVE_FC_2 (12-byte request), 0x44 FC_DRIVE_CYCLE, 0x45 search2 (17 bytes), 0x49 MoveFcVel2 (4 bytes), 0x4A MOVE_FC_CAP2 and 0x5B IS_LENS_SHIFT_CYCLE_A; first-generation items are 0x1C, 0x1D (5 bytes), 0x1F and 0x3C. ([E0648](../evidence/0648-ilce6400-bl-lens-focus-command-ids.md))
- **C36** `OFFLINE` Each MOVE_FC_2 wrapper calls 0x63D12860(0x43) -> 0x63855F80 and falls back to the 5-byte 0x1D item when it returns 0; 0x63855F94 tests bit (id-1) of the bitmap at BL_LENS_DATA+1, IDs 0x41-0x49 also require [+0x20FC]+0x20 and a clear inhibit byte at 0x6448B4A0, and a camera-side mask table at 0x6448B366 gives the final answer. ([E0648](../evidence/0648-ilce6400-bl-lens-focus-command-ids.md)) *Note: Inference (E0648 [I]): the lens's startup data selects second- or first-generation commands; the field meanings and units are not established.*
- **C37** `PHYSICAL` With a Sigma 18-50 F2.8 DC DN attached, /proc/iomem lists System RAM 0x00000000-0x3FFFFFFF and 0x80000000-0x8FFFFFFF and no process maps the ORIL window 0x6xxxxxxx, so BL_LENS_DATA is unreachable through process memory; captured libObj data/bss and heap contain no lens name strings and no key 0xC06A paired with 0x2285/0x2286, and /lens (/dev/nflasha18) holds only Sony VX*_lensfile.bin correction files. ([E0649](../evidence/0649-ilce6400-live-lens-info-linux-side-negative.md))

### <a id="dev-stream"></a>/dev/stream display and heap window

`dev.stream` | device

Display/heap mapping device: gl_common at PA 0x202e0000 (32 MiB), OSD A/B at PA 0x23a80000/0x23b16000, and the mpMemory/mpText heaps.

Aliases: `0x202e0000`

Current knowledge:

- **C19** `PHYSICAL` im.elf (PID 149) maps libObj.so text at 0x05d18000-0x0700e000 and data at 0x07016000-0x07106000, and maps /dev/stream at VA 0x08a5f000-0x0aa5f000 (32 MiB) backed by PA 0x202e0000; /dev/dmpgles2 registers are mapped at 0x0b5a2000-0x0b5c2000. ([E0073](../evidence/0073-live-hardware-ground-truth-and-a6400-boot-telemetry.md))
- **C21** `PHYSICAL` A ptrace read of im.elf's existing /dev/stream mapping returned OSD A as 614,400 bytes with 607,746 nonzero and SHA-256 7a535b09be2e370fda25091a3819289bf59d8f23e82ec0bb8030a43768c32906, which decodes to a complete PlayMemories screen; OSD B returned the identical length and SHA-256, so both buffers held the same frame. ([E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md))
- **C22** `PHYSICAL` gl_common+0x1000 (PA 0x202e1000, 1,036,800 bytes) held 604,162 nonzero bytes with SHA-256 903f6910878ea1d11dc07a5b0e47b0a86ba58ca650aa700415a8557eae100b04 and decodes as a repeated pattern, not a UI frame; the 960x540 buffer is internal, not a display surface. ([E0297](../evidence/0297-live-display-contract-and-camera-reboot.md), [E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md))

### <a id="lib-libobj"></a>libObj.so (Sugilite client and application objects)

`lib.libobj` | module

Application library that maps the OSD planes, drives the DMP SMAPH-S30 command stream, and owns the GRM/RM state.

Current knowledge:

- **C19** `PHYSICAL` im.elf (PID 149) maps libObj.so text at 0x05d18000-0x0700e000 and data at 0x07016000-0x07106000, and maps /dev/stream at VA 0x08a5f000-0x0aa5f000 (32 MiB) backed by PA 0x202e0000; /dev/dmpgles2 registers are mapped at 0x0b5a2000-0x0b5c2000. ([E0073](../evidence/0073-live-hardware-ground-truth-and-a6400-boot-telemetry.md))
- **C23** `OFFLINE` libObj.so self-identifies as DMP SMAPH-S30 (OpenGL ES 2.0) at file offset 0xFDF0F0, so the PICA200 register/ISA mapping recorded in E0081/E0082 is invalid for this device; the retained command stream uses 8-byte framing header=0xF000|(index<<16) with 566 packets in 17 runs. ([E0298](../evidence/0298-safe-osd-capture-and-sugilite-correction.md))
- **C28** `OFFLINE` The opt-in --gles-engine-model command-completion replays the physically observed 0x40000000 IRQ class after the guest submits the BAR command (BAR+0xE8=1, +0xEA=5), performs the decoded acks and consumes the ring header; it never completes a guest ctx and injects no signal. In engine11 the guest exited the 0x72B660 loop, issued a second 0x820E and parked at 0x72BAF0. ([E0314](../evidence/0314-gpes-bar-irq-contract-engine-model.md))
- **C39** `OFFLINE` The six-byte prologue 98 b5 00 af 04 46 appears 375 times in libObj executable segments, so it is not a function identity and a patch at its first match proves byte modification only. PAS_MenuSelectMode::setTouchable is at linked 0x56dcb0; its two-byte CBZ at +6 must survive, because the old four-byte NOP also overwrote the following LDR.W and left 08 31 (ADD). ([E0085](../evidence/0085-touch-hook-false-matches-and-live-disable.md), [E0086](../evidence/0086-live-touch-enodev-and-menu-instruction-audit.md))

### <a id="sys-camera-memory"></a>ILCE-6400 boot memory layout

`sys.camera-memory` | device

Kernel command line and physical memory reservations of the live body, including the reserved first MiB and the DRAM windows.

Aliases: `mem=1G@0`, `memrsv=704M@0x14000000:uc`

Current knowledge:

- **C18** `PHYSICAL` The body runs Linux 3.0.27_nl-rt106+ (SMP PREEMPT RT, armv7l) on a quad-core CXD90045 Cortex-A5 with mem=1G@0, mem=256M@0x80000000@1, memrsv=704M@0x14000000:uc, memrsv=242M@0x80e00000:uc and wbimem=0x3916000@0x20200000. ([E0073](../evidence/0073-live-hardware-ground-truth-and-a6400-boot-telemetry.md))
- **C34** `OFFLINE` -M sony-a6400,lowmem-abort=on answers PA 0x000F8000-0x000F8FFF with MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR and reproduces FSR 0x008 with 'Entering exception monitor.'; the default board backs the first MiB with RAM, so the same read passes silently. ([E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md))

### <a id="proc-osal-uipc"></a>/proc/osal/uipc registration tables

`proc.osal-uipc` | source

Live OSAL message-queue, semaphore and callback tables (1,748 lines) used to chase real producers and consumers.

Current knowledge:

- **C29** `PHYSICAL` /proc/osal/uipc on the live camera reports 836 message queues, 197 semaphores, 16 messages, 1,135 callbacks and 358 misc entries in 1,748 lines; the ubiquitous callback 0x04113c67 resolves to libMWF+0x1cc67, and the GMSGQ/GSEM tables and the LMSGQ extra columns are not decoded. ([E0313](../evidence/0313-readonly-physical-gpes-bar-and-grm-state.md))

### <a id="process-im-elf"></a>im.elf (PID 149)

`process.im-elf` | process

Main camera application; restored from the ssboot.bin hibernation snapshot rather than started with execve.

Current knowledge:

- **C19** `PHYSICAL` im.elf (PID 149) maps libObj.so text at 0x05d18000-0x0700e000 and data at 0x07016000-0x07106000, and maps /dev/stream at VA 0x08a5f000-0x0aa5f000 (32 MiB) backed by PA 0x202e0000; /dev/dmpgles2 registers are mapped at 0x0b5a2000-0x0b5c2000. ([E0073](../evidence/0073-live-hardware-ground-truth-and-a6400-boot-telemetry.md))
- **C38** `PHYSICAL` im.elf is not started with execve at power-on: the bootloader restores its address space from /system/sabin/ssboot.bin (warm.mode=2 DDR self-refresh), so /etc/ld.so.preload is not applied to im.elf, while daemons started later by shell scripts (for example bsa_server) do parse it. ([E0084](../evidence/0084-live-hardware-touch-subsystem-and-input-event-architecture.md)) *Note: The touch-scanner claims in the same record are retracted by E0085/E0086; this boot finding is independent of them.*

### <a id="tool-ro-page"></a>ro_page v2 (/dev/mem reader with SIGBUS handling)

`tool.ro-page` | tool

Single-page /dev/mem reader that installs SIGBUS/SIGSEGV handlers, so a caught bus error does not reach the exception monitor.

Aliases: `8c9f360b`, `catching=True`

Current knowledge:

- **C33** `PHYSICAL` A single-page read of PA 0x000F8000 faults with FSR 0x008 (external abort on non-linefetch). Uncaught, it reaches force_sig_info(SIGBUS), the default core-dump path and em_exception_monitor, which warm-reboots; ro_page v2 with SIGBUS handling reported 'bus error caught: signal 7' at 0x000F8000 and the camera stayed up (uptime 3,198.8 -> 3,243.9 s). Imprecise aborts and kernel-mode faults still reboot. ([E0647](../evidence/0647-ilce6400-devmem-reboot-root-cause-and-policy.md))
